attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, stated in his own voice. Hinton's argument is quoted separately and is not the claim.

semantics.note: Faithful comparative observation. The schizophrenia exception is attached to the preceding sentence in the source, but it plainly qualifies the same contrast, and 'rarely' is kept. Nothing is added or dropped.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. Wholesale invention is kept separate from minor errors, lies and jokes, 'rarely' gets no number, and the period ends at the post date. Requiring comparable evidence on both sides is reasonable.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed study published Sept 2023, before the post. It finds that 55% of GPT-3.5 and 18% of GPT-4 citations were nonexistent works. That supports the LLM half for one task family only, and it has no human comparison.

2016 systematic review of false childhood memories induced by suggestion. Laboratory induction is not everyday spontaneous fabrication, and its authors conclude susceptibility is limited. It neither establishes nor refutes 'rarely'.

TruthfulQA compares humans and models, but it measures answers that repeat misconceptions, not wholesale invention. It uses older models and a limited human baseline, so it is not a matched test of the claim.

reviews.rationale: Supporting the claim requires both halves. e1 shows LLMs recurrently fabricate substantial facts (citations) before the post. No item gives a representative human rate of unintended wholesale invention on comparable tasks. e2 measures induced memories and e3 measures misconceptions, so neither supports nor contradicts the human half. The comparison is not settled by the packet.
